SBR line breaking

The single-pass deterministic line-break contract, break statuses and zone dispatch.

SBR (SUAS-003) is a single-pass deterministic line-breaking engine over the full 64-bit SuperUnicode space (sucs_ex_char_t). Each adjacent pair resolves to a break status via a transition matrix — mandatory, allowed, prohibited, or the CJK/numeric alphanumeric break — in constant time, with zero allocation.

Status Meaning
MUST_BREAK Mandatory line boundary (e.g. after a control).
CAN_BREAK Allowed / opportunistic boundary.
NO_BREAK Prohibited boundary.
ALPHANUM_BREAK Mandatory CJK/numeric alphabetic break.
  • Zone dispatch — Unicode Bridge (curated UAX #14 break classes + transition matrix), SCP (Explicit Break Markers), Native SUCS (O(1) high-bit range bitmask word test), ExtSUCS (neutral gap).
  • Explicit SCP Break Markers — 0x00110020 MANDATORY, 0x00110021 PROHIBITED, 0x00110022 OPPORTUNISTIC — absolute overrides.
  • Invisible formatting — U+200B ZWSP offers a break; U+2060 WJ prohibits on either side.
  • Zero heap allocation — O(1) transition-matrix lookup, suitable for freestanding C99.

Formalized in SUAS-003. Source of truth: docs/suas/SUAS-003-sbr.md.
